AST02.ruling: Refuse the alert counts as positive supply: alerts (and per-visit alert rates) are the abundant row unit, while the follow-up decision binds on distinct transients/DIAObjects. Re-count positive supply as clustered objects eligible for a spectrum and report raw beside clustered.
AST02.rule: P3 (never count rows; positive supply counted at the abundant unit); global 1 population field

AST5-02.ruling: Refuse the directional claim: the 0.018 purity difference is below the 0.045 MDE, and no paired sigma_d exists. Write a no-claim with MDE and chance baseline beside the effect, stating only that no effect larger than about 0.045 is hiding; the production choice is not evidence of superiority.
AST5-02.rule: A4 (refuse directional claim at or below MDE); global 5

AST03.ruling: Accept the cluster-structure axis: raw 11193 beside clustered 11183 with overstatement 0.089 percent, both must-merge and must-not-merge controls run and all rows accounted for. Record the number and continue counting the remaining axes.
AST03.rule: P3 cluster structure, raw beside clustered

AST-P2-02.ruling: Refuse the floor pricing: all three figures come from the set used to select the recurrent model's architecture and epoch, and the floor is priced against the weakest classical tools while a stronger template tool was not run. Re-price on the held-out 1,011 spectra against the strongest classical alternative before stating a floor share.
AST-P2-02.rule: P2 provenance record; global 1 (adjudicator and population fields)

AST3-04.ruling: Admit the item: first detection postdates every published subject cutoff, the undated subject was removed and recorded, the item text carries no answer, the label arrives after sealing from a non-automated reporter, and the exposure ruling is written.

AST01.ruling: Refuse to adopt 30 arcsec: the curve shows no saturation bound (no step gains more than 0.3 percent) and there is no separation column, so the cut is not bounded by measurement, and at 30 arcsec 39 pairs of distinct supernovae are merged. Add the separation signal, rerun the sweep and choose a cut the curve bounds, with looser and tighter sensitivity reported, or mark tau UNDEMONSTRATED.
AST01.rule: D3 (choose cut by measurement bounded by saturation and separation; tau.py refuses when the curve does not bound one)

ASTC-01.ruling: Admissible as paired: both arms run on the same 6,045 objects with the same folds and the 16 exclusions applied identically, so the denominator is common. Score paired per object/fold with coverage stated.
ASTC-01.rule: A3 score paired on a common denominator; global 4 not triggered

AST-P2-03.ruling: Accept as a prior floor estimate: clustered, grouped CV, label-permutation and temporal controls reported, labelled as prior rather than built, and no ceiling claimed. Record with its provenance; the share of ceiling remains to be stated against a ceiling before P2 closes or advances on it.
AST-P2-03.rule: P2 prior floor estimate with provenance record

AST4-02.ruling: Refuse '7 of 15 verified on Rubin': ELAsTiCC simulation scores are an adjacent referent, all 7 were trained only on simulations, and ATAT, ORACLE full and ParSNIP LSST need fields the lsst.v11_1 packet lacks. Report tool coverage as zero verified on real Rubin inputs, with those channels marked structurally unavailable on the supplied input.
AST4-02.rule: P3 tool coverage axis (channel structurally unavailable); global 1 referent/source

ASTC-02.ruling: Accept checkpoint identity: the served file's locally computed sha256 matches the hub's object id for the revision, and a content hash satisfies the card's revision-or-hash field. Record the hash on the card.
ASTC-02.rule: I3 served checkpoint with revision or content hash

AST3-03.ruling: Refuse zero exposure: a missing date column and refused access make the axis undemonstrated, not zero, and the archived 2024-12-08 copy shows 6166 labels public before every subject cutoff. Report at least 6166 exposed units (with every labeled object predating the latest cutoffs) and disclose contamination.
AST3-03.rule: P3 contamination exposure axis; global 1 and 11 (undemonstrated never zero)

AST4-03.ruling: Check (b) passes: ParSNIP decode_spectra is a generator on an agent-set condition, and the redshift likelihood and SALT3 chi2 under an agent-bounded hypothesis are scorers, all pinned. The production pipeline's composition is irrelevant to whether the tool inventory holds a role below the encoder/predictor line.
AST4-03.rule: manifest.md checks at ratification (b): at least one role below the encoder and predictor line

AST3-01.ruling: Refuse recording 7843 as spectroscopic labels: the type column mixes measured spectroscopic truth with automated RNN classifications, light-curve-only classifications and reused reports, and no column separates them. Mark the label-source slot UNDEMONSTRATED until measured labels can be separated (e.g. from name-server reports with reporter/date), name the dependent stages, and escalate.
AST3-01.rule: D4 label source (measured truth vs annotation from predictions); global 1 referent

AST5-01.ruling: Refuse '93% vs ~97%': the figures use different populations, windows and referents (bright extragalactic vs any extragalactic) and the scanner figure is internally inconsistent (96.7 vs 95.6). Report them as not comparable and require paired scoring on a common item set and definition.
AST5-01.rule: A3 (arm means on different denominators are not a comparison); global 4

AST3-02.ruling: Refuse admission: the item text is the classification report and an SN-prefixed designation, so the answer appears in the item's own source, and the 2021 report predates every subject cutoff so no exposure exception applies. Rebuild the item from pre-classification data with a neutral identifier.

AST4-01.ruling: Refuse deleting the disagreement list: write the card fields from the pinned code but list every paper-versus-code disagreement (dropout, learning rate, input dimension) rather than reconciling them silently.
AST4-01.rule: I3 (list every disagreement rather than reconciling; non-optional disagreement list)

AST-P2-04.ruling: Refuse AUC 0.967 as the floor: redshift and redshift-derived absolute magnitude exist only for already-classified objects, so the features are unavailable at the decision and the number measures an adjacent, leaked quantity. State the floor from decision-time features (0.798 tier) with a full provenance record.
AST-P2-04.rule: P2 floor with provenance record; global 1 referent

AST04.ruling: Refuse amending the frozen label map after the count: it widens a definition after a low count and changes a rule post-count, which invalidates the count. Report the 9/9 test side low; any rule change requires re-registering the corpus and rerunning the counting stages.
AST04.rule: D2 (a rule that changes after a count invalidates the count); global 9

AST-P2-01.ruling: Close on headroom: the classical light-curve-fit floor already takes the multi-class ceiling (0.71 vs 0.71) and 0.92 of 0.95 on binary Ia, with only an unpaired fold spread behind the gap, and the channel is an encoder needing no agent. Do not build the benchmark around the learned representation.
AST-P2-01.rule: P2 (closes the candidate when the floor already takes the ceiling)

AST4-04.ruling: Refuse mounting both channels without an exposure ruling: the encoder's checkpoint was fine-tuned on BTS objects and the classifier's labels are the BTS scanner decisions the benchmark governs, so items drawn from pre-June-2024 BTS objects are exposed to the channels themselves. Count contamination per channel against training membership, exclude overlapping items or unmount the channels, and write the exposure ruling.
